ἀγαθός, -ή, -όν,
  [in LXX chiefly for טוֹב;]
in general, good, in physical and in moral sense, used of persons, things, acts, conditions, etc., applied to that which is regarded as "perfect in its kind, so as to produce pleasure and satisfaction,... that which, in itself good, is also at once for the good and the advantage of him who comes in contact with it" (Cremer, 3): γῆ, Lk 8:8; δένδρον, Mt 7:18; καρδία, Lk 8:15; δόσις, Ja 1:17; μέρις, Lk 10:42; ἔργον (freq. in Pl.), Phl 1:6; ἐλπίς, II Th 2:16; θησαυρός, Mt 12:35; μνεία, I Th 3:6 (cf. II Mac 7:20); as subst., τὸ ἀ., that which is morally good, beneficial, acceptable to God, Ro 12:2; ἐργάζεσθαι τὸ ἀ, Ro 2:10, Eph 4:28; πράσσειν, Ro 9:11, II Co 5:10; διώκειν, I Th 5:15; μιμεῖσθαι, III Jo 11; κολλᾶσθαι τῷ ἀ., Ro 12:9; ερωτᾶν περὶ τοῦ ἀ., Mt 19:17; διάκονος εἰς τὸ ἀ., Ro 13:4; τὸ ἀ. σου, thy favour, benefit, Phm 14; pl., τὰ ἀ., of goods, possessions, Lk 12:18; of spiritual benefits, Ro 10:15, He 9:11, 10:1. ἀ. is opp. to πονηρός, Mt 5:45, 20:5; κακός, Ro 7:19; φαῦλος, Ro 9:11, II Co 5:10 (cf. MM, VGT, s.v.).
  SYN.: καλός, δίκαιος. κ. properly refers to goodliness as manifested in form: ἀ. to inner excellence (cf. the cl. καλὸς κἀγαθός and ἐν καρδίᾳ κ. καὶ ἀ., Lk 8:15). In Ro 5:7, where it is contrasted with δ., ἀ. implies a kindliness and attractiveness not necessarily possessed by the δίκαιος, who merely measures up to a high standard of rectitude (cf. ἀγαθωσύνη).

αἰών, -ῶνος, ὁ,
  [in LXX chiefly for עַד,עוֹלָם;]
1. in cl., like Lat. aevum (LS, MM, VGT, s.v.), a space of time, as, a lifetime, generation, period of history, an indefinitely long period; in NT of an indefinitely long period, an age, eternity, usually c. prep. (MM, VGT);
   (a) of the past: ἀπ’ αἰ. (cf. Heb. מֵעוֹלָם), Lk 1:70;
   (b) of the future: εἰς τ. αἰ. (cf. לְעוֹלָם), forever, Mt 21:19; id., c. neg., never, Jo 4:14; more strongly, εἰς τὸν αἰ. τοῦ αἰ., He 1:8(LXX); εἰς τοὺς αἰ., Mt 6:13; εἰς τοὺς αἰ. τῶν αἰ. (cf. Is 45:17, עַד־עוֹלְמֵי עַד), Ro 16:27, LT; cf. also Eph 3:21, II Pe 3:18, Ju 25, Re 14:11.
2. οἱ αἰ., the worlds, the universe, "the sum of the periods of time, including all that is manifested in them": He 1:2 11:3 (cf. I Ti 1:17, where τῶν αἰ. are prob. "the ages or world-periods which when summed up make eternity".
3. the present age (Heb. הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה): ὁ αἰ., Mt 13:22; ὁ αἰ. οὗτος, Mt 12:32; ὁ νῦν αἰ., I Ti 6:17; ὁ ἐνεστὼς αἰ., Ga 1:4; similarly, of the time after Christ's second coming (הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא), ὁ αἰ. ἐκεῖνος, Lk 20:35; ὁ αἰ. μέλλων, Mt 12:32; ὁ αἰ. ὁ ἐρχόμενος, Mk 10:30.
  SYN.: κόσμος, the ordered universe, the scheme of material things; οἰκουμένη, the inhabited earth; in contrast with both of which αἰ. is the world under aspects of time (cf. Westc. on He 1:2; Tr., Syn., §lix; Thayer, s.v., αἰ.; Cremer, 74, 620; MM, VGT).

articulos.texto:
*† ἁρπαγμός, οῦ, ὁ
  (< ἁρπάζω);
1. prop., acc., to the rule of its formation (Bl., § 27, 2), actively, the act of seizing, robbery (Plut., de Puer. Educ., p. 12A), Phl 2:6, AV (Waterland, Works, II, 108; Cremer, 649 f.; Meyer, in l.; cf. also JThS, July, 1909, April, 1911; MM, s.v.).
2. Passively = ἅρπαγμα (Ez 22:25, of a lion's prey, טֶרֶף), a thing seized, hence, a prize: Phl 2:6, RV (Lft., Ellic., ICC, in l.; Donaldson, NCrat., 450 ff.; and esp. Gifford, The Incarnation, 59-71, and reff. in DB, ii, 835 B). The lexical data favour the active meaning, but as they also admit the possibility of the alternative, most modern expositors have accepted the latter as seeming to suit the logic of the passage better. The lexical difficulty, however, remains (MM, s.v., esp. the last ref.). As to the usage of St. Paul, he seems inclined to adopt the -μα form where it is appropriate (e.g. Ro 11:9, where cf. LXX; I Co 13:9, II Co 1:9), and there is certainly a presumption in favour of the active meaning here from the fact that he does not use the LXX ἅρπαγμα. Suggestions looking to a fresh exegesis are given in JThS, July, 1909, April, 1911.†

articulos.texto:
ἀγαπάω, -ῶ,
  [in LXX chiefly for אהב;]
to love, to feel and exhibit esteem and goodwill to a person, to prize and delight in a thing.
   1. Of human affection, to men: τ. πλησίον, Mt 5:43; τ. ἐχθρούς, ib. 44; to Christ, Jo 8:42; to God, Mt 22:37; c. acc. rei, Lk 11:43, Jo 12:43, Eph 5:25, II Tim 4:8, 10, He 1:9, I Pe 2:17, 3:10, II Pe 2:15, I Jo 2:15, Re 12:11.
   2. Of divine love;
      (a) God's love: to men, Ro 8:37; to Christ, Jo 3:35;
      (b) Christ's love: to men, Mk 10:21; to God, Jo 14:31; c. cogn. acc., Jo 17:26, Eph 2:4.
  SYN.: φιλέω. From its supposed etymology (Thayer, LS; but v. also Boisacq) ἀ. is commonly understood properly to denote love based on esteem (diligo), as distinct from that expressed by φιλέω (amo), spontaneous natural affection, emotional and unreasoning. If this distinction holds, ἀ. is fitly used in NT of Christian love to God and man, the spiritual affection which follows the direction of the will, and which, therefore, unlike that feeling which is instinctive and unreasoned, can be commanded as a duty. (Cf. ἀγάπη, and v. Tr., Syn. §xii; Cremer, 9, 592; and esp. MM, VGT, s.v.)

* ἀνθρωποκτόνος, -ον
  (< κτείνω, to kill),
a murderer, manslayer (Eur.; v. MM, VGT, s.v.): Jo 8:44, I Jo 3:15.†
  SYN.: φονεύς, ἀνδροφόνος (v. Tr., Syn, § lxxxiii).

articulos.texto:
† ἀγάπη, -ης, ἡ
  [in LXX for אַהֲבָה, which is also rendered by ἀγάπησις and φιλία;]
love, goodwill, esteem. Outside of bibl. and eccl. books, there is no clear instance (with Deiss., LAE, 18:4, 70:2, cf. the same writer in Constr. Quar., ii, 4; and with MM, VGT, s.v., cf. Dr. Moulton in Exp. Times, xxvi, 3, 139). In NT, like ἀγαπάω, -ῶ,
   1. Of men's love:
      (a) to one another, Jo 13:35;
      (b) to God, I Jo 2:5.
   2. Of divine love;
      (a) God's love: to men, Ro 5:8; to Christ, Jo 17:26;
      (b) Christ's love to men: Ro 8:35.
   3. In pl., love feasts: Ju 12 (DB, iii, 157).
  SYN.: φιλία. ἀ., signifying properly (v.s. ἀγαπάω) love which chooses its object, is taken over from LXX, where its connotation is more general, into NT, and there used exclusively to express that spiritual bond of love between God and man and between man and man, in Christ, which is characteristic of Christianity. It is thus distinct from φιλία, friendship (Ja 4:4 only), στοργή, natural affection (in NT only in compounds, v.s. ἄστοργος) and ἔρως, sexual love, which is not used in NT, its place being taken by ἐπιθυμία. (Cf. ἀγαπάω; and v. Abbott, Essays, 70f.; DB, vol. i., 555; Cremer, 13, 593; MM, VGT, s.v.).

articulos.texto:
ἀλλά (ἀλλ’ usually bef. α and υ, often bef. ε and η, rarely bef. ο and ω, never bef. ι; Tdf., Pr., 93 f.; WH, App., 146),
  adversative particle,
stronger than δέ; prop. neuter pl. of ἄλλος, used adverbially, with changed accent; hence prop. otherwise, on the other hand (cf. Ro 3:31);
   1. opposing a previous negation, but: οὐ (μὴ)... ἀ., Mt 5:15, 17 Mk 5:39, Jo 7:16, al.; rhetorically subordinating but not entirely negativing what precedes, οὐ... ἀ., not so much... as, Mk 9:37, Mt 10:20, Jo 12:44, al.; with ellipse of the negation, Mt 11:7-9, Ac 19:2, I Co 3:6 6:11 7:7, II Co 7:1, Ga 2:3, al.; in opposition to a foregoing pos. sentence, ἀ. οὐ, Mt 24:6, I Co 10:23;
οὐ μόνον... ἀ. καί, Jo 5:18, Ro 1:32, al.; elliptically, after a negation, ἀ. ἵνα, Mk 14:49, Jo 1:8 9:3, al.; = εἰ μή (Bl., §77, 13; M, Pr., 241; but cf. WM, §iii, 10), Mt 20:23, Mk 4:22.
   2. Without previous negation, to express opposition, interruption, transition, etc., but: Jo 16:20 12:27, Ga 2:14; before commands or requests, Ac 10:20 26:16, Mt 9:18, Mk 9:22, al.; to introduce an accessory idea, II Co 7:11; in the apodosis after a condition or concession with εἰ, ἐάν, εἴπερ, yet, still, at least, Mk 14:29, I Co 9:2, II Co 4:16, Col 2:5, al.; after μέν, Ac 4:17, Ro 14:20, I Co 14:17; giving emphasis to the following
      clause, ἀλλ’ ἔρχεται ὥρα, yea, etc., Jo 16:2; so with neg., ἀλλ’ οὐδέ, nay, nor yet, Lk 23:15.
   3. Joined with other particles (a practice which increases in late writers; Simcox, LNT, 166), ἀ. γε, yet at least, Lk 24:21, I Co 9:2; ἄ ἤ., save only, except, Lk 12:51, II Co 1:13; ἀ. μὲν οὖν, Phl 3:8 (on this usage, v. MM, VGT, s.v.).

G40.definicion_es: sagrado (físicamente, puro, moralmente irreprensible o religioso, ceremonialmente, consagrado)

articulos.texto:
ἅγιος, -α, ον
  (< τό ἅγός, religious awe; ἅζω, to venerate),
  [in LXX chiefly for קֹ֫דֶשׁ;]
primarily, dedicated to the gods, sacred (Hdt.; rare in Att., never in Hom., Hes. and Trag., who use ἁγνός), hence, holy, characteristic of God, separated to God, worthy of veneration.
   1. Its highest application is to God himself, in his purity, majesty, and glory: Lk 1:49, Jo 17:11, Re 4:8. Hence
      (a) of things and places which have a claim to reverence as sacred to God, e.g. the Temple: Mt 24:15, He 9:1;
      (b) of persons employed by him, as angels: I Th 3:13; prophets, Lk 1:70; apostles, Eph 3:5.
   2. Applied to persons as separated to God's service:
      (a) of Christ, Mk 1:24, Jo 6:69, Ac 4:30;
      (b) of Christians, Ac 9:13, Ro 1:7, He 6:10, Re 5:8.
   3. In the moral sense of sharing God's purity: Mk 6:20, Jo 17:11, Ac 3:14, Re 3:7.
   4. Of pure, clean sacrifices and offerings: I Co 7:14, Eph 1:4.
  SYN.: ἁγνός, pure, both in ceremonial and spiritual sense; ἱερός (sacer), sacred, that which is inviolable because of its (external) relation to God; ὅσιος (sanctus as opp. to nefas), that which is based on everlasting ordinances of right. (Cf. Tr., Syn., §lxxxviii; DB, ii, 399 f.; Cremer, 34, 594-601; MM, VGT, s.v.)
articulos.texto_es:
ἅγιος, -α, ον
  (< τό ἅγός, religioso temor reverente; ἅζω, venerar),
  [en LXX sobre todo para קֹ֫דֶשׁ;]
en primer lugar, dedicado al dioses, sagrado (Hdt.; raro en Att., nunca en Hom., Hes. y Trag., quien uso ἁγνός), de ahí, santo, característico de Dios, separado a Dios, digno de veneración.
   1. su aplicación suprema es a Dios sí mismo, en su pureza, majestad, y gloria: Lk 1:49, Jo 17:11, Re 4:8. de ahí
      ( a) de cosas y lugares que tener un reclamar a reverencia como sagrado a Dios, por ejemplo el templo: Mt 24:15, él 9:1;
      ( b) de personas empleado por él, como ángeles: I Th 3:13; profetas, Lk 1:70; apóstoles, Eph 3:5.
   2. aplicado a personas como separado a God's servicio:
      ( a) de Cristo, Mk 1:24, Jo 6:69, Ac 4:30;
      ( b) de cristianos, Ac 9:13, Ro 1:7, él 6:10, Re 5:8.
   3. en el moral sentido de compartir God's pureza: Mk 6:20, Jo 17:11, Ac 3:14, Re 3:7.
   4. de puro, sacrificios limpios y ofrendas: I Co 7:14, Eph 1:4.
  SINÓNIMOS: ἁγνός, puro, ambos en ceremonial y sentido espiritual; ἱερός (sacer), sagrado, lo que es inviolable a causa de su (externo) relación a Dios; ὅσιος (sanctus como opuesto a a nefas), lo que es basado sobre ordenanzas eternos de derecho. (Cf. Tr., Syn., § lxxxviii; DB, ii, 399 femenino; Cremer, 34, 594-601; MM, VGT, s. v.)

aguardar o esperar con ansia (Lft., notas, 149; MM, VGT, s. v.): absoluto, I Peal 3:20; con acusativo de la cosa, Ro 8:19, 23, 25, I Co 1:7, Ga 5:5; con acusativo de la persona, Phl 3:20, él 9:28.†

G658.definicion_es: completar del todo, es decir, consumar

articulos.texto:
** ἀπο-τελέω, -ῶ
  [in LXX: I Es 5:73, I Mac 15:39*;]
to bring to an end, complete, accomplish (cf. MM, s.v.): Lk 13:32, Ja 1:15.†
articulos.texto_es:
** ἀπο-τελέω, -ῶ
  [en LXX: I Es 5:73, I Mac 15:39*;]
traer a un fin, completo, llevar cabo (compárese MM, s. v.): Lk 13:32, Ja 1:15.†

G578.definicion: to look away from everything else, i.e. (figuratively) intently regard
G578.definicion_es: mirar lejos de todo otro, es decir, (figuradamente) con fijeza considerar

articulos.glosa: to look away from all else at one object
articulos.texto:
ἀπο-βλέπω,
  [in LXX for פּנה, etc.;]
to look away from all else at one object; hence, to look steadfastly: He 11:26 (cf. ἀφοράω).†

† βδελυκτός, ή, -όν
  (< βδελύσσω),
  [in LXX: Pr 17:15 (תּוֹעֵבָה), Si 41:5, II Mac 1:27*;]
abominable, detestable: Tit 1:16 (Cremer, 137).†

G504.origen: de G1 (Α) (como negativa partícula) y G5204 (ὕδωρ)

articulos.texto:
ἄνυδρος, -ον
  (< ἀ- neg., ὕδωρ),
  [in LXX for צִיָּה, יְשִׁימוֹן (γῆ ἄ), etc.;]
waterless: τόποι, Mt 12:43, Lk 11:24; πηγαί, II Pe 2:17; νεφέλαι, Ju 12 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

G58.definicion: probably akin to G1453 (ἐγείρω)); properly, the town-square (as a place of public resort); by implication, a market or thoroughfare
G58.definicion_es: probablemente afín a G1453 (ἐγείρω); propiamente, la plaza de la ciudad (como lugar de concurrencia pública); por implicación, un mercado o una vía pública

articulos.texto:
ἀγορά, -ας, ἡ (< ἀγείρω, to bring together)
  [in LXX for עִזָּבוֹן, שׁוּק;]
1. an assembly (Hom., Xen., al.).
2. a place of assembly, a public place or forum, a market-place (Hom., Thuc, al.; LXX): Mt 11:16 20:2 23:7, Mk 6:56 (cf. MM, VGT, s.v., ἀγυιά) 7:4 (Bl., §46, 7) 12:38, Lk 7:32 (Bl., §46, 7) 11:43 20:46, Ac 16:19 17:7 (Cremer, 59; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

G405.origen: de un derivado de un compuesto de G435 (ἀνήρ) y G4228 (πούς)
G405.definicion: an enslaver (as bringing men to his feet)
G405.definicion_es: un esclavizador (como quien pone a los hombres a sus pies)

articulos.texto:
* ἀνδραποδιστής, -οῦ, ὁ
  (< ἀνδράποδον, a slave, captured in war),
a slave-dealer, kidnapper: I Ti 1:10 (v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

G193.origen: de G1 (Α) (como negativa partícula) y G2904 (κράτος)
G193.definicion_es: sin fuerza, es decir, sin dominio de sí

articulos.texto:
ἀκρατής, -ές
  (< κράτος),
  [in LXX: Pr 27:20*;]
   (a) powerless, impotent;
   (b) in moral sense, lacking self-control, incontinent: II Ti 3:3.†

ἀ-μέμπτως,
    adv.
  (< ἄμεμπτος),
  [in LXX: Es 3:13*;]
blamelessly (Lft., Notes, 28, 89; MM, VGT, s.v. -ος): I Th 2:10 3:13 WH mg., 5:23.†

Αἰνέας, -οῦ, ὁ,
Æneas: Ac 9:33, 34.†

** ἀπο-φεύγω,
  [in LXX: Si 22:22*;]
to flee from, escape: c. acc., II Pe 2:18, 20; c. gen., II Pe 1:4.†
articulos.texto_es:
** ἀπο-φεύγω,
  [en LXX: Si 22:22*;]
huir de, escapar: con acusativo, II Peal 2:18, 20; con genitivo, II Peal 1:4.†

G830.origen: de G846 (αὐτός) y lo mismo que G140 (αἱρετίζω)
G830.definicion_es: escogido por uno mismo, es decir, (por implicación) voluntario
G830.usos: of own accord, willing of self

articulos.texto:
** αὐθαίρετος, -ον
  (< αὐτός, αἱρέομαι),
  [in Sm.: Ex 35:5, 22*;]
1. self-chosen.
2. of one's own accord: II Co 8:3, 17.†

G932.definicion: properly, royalty, i.e. (abstractly) rule, or (concretely) a realm (literally or figuratively)
G932.definicion_es: propiamente, realeza, es decir, (en abstracto) gobernar, o (en concreto) un reino (literal o figuradamente)

articulos.texto:
βασιλεία, -ας, ἡ
  (< βασιλεύω),
  [in LXX chiefly for מַמְלָכָה מַלְכוּת;]
1. prop. abstract, sovereignty, royal power, dominion: Lk 1:33 22:29, Jo 18:36, Ac 1:6, He 1:8, I Co 15:24; λαβεῖν β., Lk 19:12, 15, Re 17:12; δοῦναι τὴν, Re 17:17; ἔχειν β., Re 17:18; ἔρχεσθαι ἐν τ. (εἰς τὴν) β., Mt 16:28, Lk 23:42; β. τ. θεοῦ, Re 12:10.
2. By meton., concrete (MM, Exp., x),
   (a) a kingdom, the territory or people over whom the king rules (Es 5:3, al.): Mt 4:8 12:25, 26 24:7, Mk 3:24 6:23, Lk 4:5, He 11:33, al.;
   (b) the royal majesty (cf. our phrase His Majesty), the king himself (τ. σπέρμα τῆς β., IV Ki 11:1).
3. In LXX (Wi 6:5, To 13:1, al.), Targ. and NT, of the Messianic rule and kingdom, ἡ β. τ. θεοῦ, τ. οὐρανῶν (Heb. מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם, Aram. מַלְכוּתָא דִשׁמַיָּא; v. Dalman, Words, 91-147; Cremer, 132, 658), the kingdom of God (on the equivalence of the two phrases, v. Dalman, op. cit., 93, 218 f.); τ. θεοῦ, Mt 6:33 12:28, al.; τ. οὐρανῶν, Mt 3:2 4:17, al.; τ. Χριστοῦ (מַלִכוּת דִמְשִׁיחא, Targ. Jon. on Is 53:10), Eph 5:5; τ. κυρίου, II Pe 1:11, Re 11:15; τ. Δαυείδ, Mk 11:10; absol., ἡ β., Mt 4:23, Ja 2:5, al. The kingdom is regarded as present: Mt 11:12, Lk 17:21, Ro 14:17, al.; as that which is to be consummated in the future, Mt 6:10, Mk 9:1, Jo 3:5, II Pe 1:11, al. Noteworthy phrases are: ζητεῖν τὴν β., Mt 6:33; δέχεσθαι, Mk 10:15; κλρονομεῖν, Mt 25:34; διδόναι, Lk
    12:32; παραλαμβάνειν, He 12:28; αὐτῶν (τοιούτων) ἐστὶν ἡ β., Mt 5:3, 10 19:14, Mk 10:14, Lk 18:16; διὰ τὴν β., Mt 19:12; ἕνεκεν τῆς β., Lk 18:29; εὐαγγελίζεσθαι, κηρύσσειν, διαγγέλλειν τὴν β., Lk 4:43 9:2, 60; ἤγγικεν ἡ β., Mt 3:2, Mk 1:15; κλεῖς τῆς β., Mt 16:19; κλείειν τὴν β., Mt 23:14; υἱοὶ τῆς β., Mt 8:12 13:38 (cf. Cremer, 132, 658).
articulos.texto_es:
βασιλεία, -ας, ἡ
  (< βασιλεύω),
  [en LXX sobre todo para מַמְלָכָה מַלְכוּת;]
1. puntal. abstracto, soberanía, poder real, dominio: Lk 1:33 22:29, Jo 18:36, Ac 1:6, él 1:8, I Co 15:24; λαβεῖν β., Lk 19:12, 15, Re 17:12; δοῦναι τὴν, Re 17:17; ἔχειν β., Re 17:18; ἔρχεσθαι ἐν τ. (εἰς τὴν) β., Mt 16:28, Lk 23:42; β. τ. θεοῦ, Re 12:10.
2. por metonimia., concreto( MM, Exp., x),
   ( a) un reino, el territorio o pueblo sobre a quien el rey reglas (Es 5:3, y otros): Mt 4:8 12:25, 26 24:7, Mk 3:24 6:23, Lk 4:5, él 11:33, y otros;
   ( b) la majestad real (compárese nuestro frase su majestad), el rey sí mismo (τ. σπέρμα τῆς β., IV Ki 11:1).
3. en LXX (Wi 6:5, a 13:1, y otros), Targ. y NT, del Messianic gobernar y reino, ἡ β. τ. θεοῦ, τ. οὐρανῶν (hebreo מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם, arameo מַלְכוּתָא דִשׁמַיָּא; véase Dalman, palabras, 91-147; Cremer, 132, 658), el reino de Dios (sobre la equivalencia del dos frases, véase Dalman, obra citado, 93, 218 femenino); τ. θεοῦ, Mt 6:33 12:28, y otros; τ. οὐρανῶν, Mt 3:2 4:17, y otros; τ. Χριστοῦ (מַלִכוּת דִמְשִׁיחא, Targ. Jon. sobre es 53:10), Eph 5:5; τ. κυρίου, II Peal 1:11, Re 11:15; τ. Δαυείδ, Mk 11:10; absoluto, ἡ β., Mt 4:23, Ja 2:5, y otros el reino es considerado como presente: Mt 11:12, Lk 17:21, Ro 14:17, y otros; como lo que es ser consumado en el futuro, Mt 6:10, Mk 9:1, Jo 3:5, II Peal 1:11, y otros frases notables son: ζητεῖν τὴν β., Mt 6:33; δέχεσθαι, Mk 10:15; κλρονομεῖν, Mt 25:34; διδόναι, Lk
    12:32; παραλαμβάνειν, él 12:28; αὐτῶν (τοιούτων) ἐστὶν ἡ β., Mt 5:3, 10 19:14, Mk 10:14, Lk 18:16; διὰ τὴν β., Mt 19:12; ἕνεκεν τῆς β., Lk 18:29; εὐαγγελίζεσθαι, κηρύσσειν, διαγγέλλειν τὴν β., Lk 4:43 9:2, 60; ἤγγικεν ἡ β., Mt 3:2, Mk 1:15; κλεῖς τῆς β., Mt 16:19; κλείειν τὴν β., Mt 23:14; υἱοὶ τῆς β., Mt 8:12 13:38 (compárese Cremer, 132, 658).

articulos.texto:
ἄγνοια, -ας, ἡ
  (< ἀγνοέω),
  [in LXX chiefly for אָשָׁם, שְׁגָגָה;]
ignorance: Ac 3:17 17:30, Eph 4:18 (with sense of wilful blindness; cf. MM, VGT, s.v.), I Pe 1:14.†

G525.definicion: to change away, i.e. release, (reflexively) remove
G525.definicion_es: cambiar lejos, es decir, soltar, (reflexivamente) quitar

articulos.texto:
ἀπ-αλλάσσω,
  [in LXX for סוּר hi., etc.;]
to remove, release: He 2:15; pass., to depart: Ac 19:12; in legal sense (MM, VGT, s.v.), seq. ἀπό, c. gen. pers., to be quit of: Lk 12:58 (Cremer, 90, 632).†

ἀνα-ζητέω, -ῶ
  [in LXX: Jb 3:4 (דרשׁ), Jb 10:6 (בּקשׁ pi.), II Mac 13:21*;]
to look for or seek carefully ("specially of searching for human beings, with an implication of difficulty": MM, VGT, s.v.): Lk 2:44, 45, Ac 11:25.†

αἰνέω, -ῶ
  (< αἶνος), poët., Ion. and late prose (MM, VGT, s.v.) for cl. ἐπαινέω,
  [in LXX chiefly for הלל, ידה;]
to praise: c. acc., τ. θεόν, Lk 2:13, 20 19:37 24:53, Ac 2:47 3:8, 9, Ro 15:11; c. dat., τ. Θεῷ (Je 20:13, al. for הִלֵּל לְ; v. Field, Notes, 245), Re 19:5.†
  SYN.: ἐξομολογέω, εὐλογέω, εὐχαριστέω, μακαρίζω (v. DCG, i, 211).

G501.definicion: to bale up (properly, bilge water), i.e. dip water (with a bucket, pitcher, etc.)
G501.definicion_es: achicar (propiamente, el agua de sentina), es decir, sacar agua (con un cubo, un cántaro, etc.)

articulos.texto:
ἀντλέω, -ῶ
  (< ἄντλος, bilge-water in a hold),
  [in LXX for שׁאב, etc.;]
1. prop., to bale out.
2. Generally, to draw water: absol., Jo 2:8 4:15; ὕδωρ, Jo 2:9 4:7 (on its use of the water made wine, v. DCG, ii, 815a; MM, VGT, s.v.; Field, Notes, 84 f.).†

G571.origen: de G1 (Α) (como negativa partícula) y G4103 (πιστός)
G571.definicion: (actively) disbelieving, i.e. without Christian faith (specially, a heathen); (passively) untrustworthy (person), or incredible (thing)
G571.definicion_es: (en activo) incrédulo, es decir, sin fe cristiana (especialmente, un pagano); (en pasivo) indigno de confianza (dicho de una persona), o increíble (dicho de una cosa)
G571.usos: that believeth not, faithless, incredible thing, infidel, unbeliever(-ing)

articulos.texto:
ἄ-πιστος, -ον
  (< ἀ- neg., πιστός),
  [in LXX: Pr 17:6 28:25, Is 17:10*;]
(a) of things, incredible: Ac 26:8;
(b) of persons, without faith or trust, unbelieving: Mt 17:17, Mk 9:19, Lk 9:41 12:46, Jo 20:27, Tit 1:15, Re 21:8; specif., of unbelievers as opp. to Christians: I Co 6:6 7:12-15 10:27 14:22-24, II Co 4:4 6:14, 15, I Ti 5:8 (cf. Lft., Notes, 265; Cremer, 491).†

G683.definicion: to push off, figuratively, to reject
G683.usos: cast away, put away (from), thrust away (from)

articulos.texto:
ἀπ-ωθέω, -ῶ,
  [in LXX for זנח, מאס, etc.;]
to thrust away. Mid., to thrust away from oneself, refuse, reject: c. acc. pers. (MM, s.v.), Ac 7:27, 39 13:46, Ro 11:1, 2, I Ti 1:19.†
articulos.texto_es:
ἀπ-ωθέω, -ῶ,
  [en LXX para זנח, מאס, etc.;]
empujar lejos. Mid., empujar lejos de a sí mismo, rehusar, rechazar: con acusativo de la persona( MM, s. v.), Ac 7:27, 39 13:46, Ro 11:1, 2, I Ti 1:19.†

G769.definicion: feebleness (of mind or body); by implication, malady; morally, frailty
G769.definicion_es: debilidad (de la mente o del cuerpo); por implicación, enfermedad; moralmente, fragilidad

articulos.texto:
ἀσθένεια, -ας, ἡ
  (< ἀσθενής),
  [in LXX for
    כּשׁל, etc.;]
weakness, frailty, sickness: Lk 13:11, 12, Jo 11:4, Ac 28:9, Ro 6:19 8:26, II Co 11:30 13:4, Ga 4:13 (MM, s.v.), He 5:2 7:28 11:34; ἐν ἀ., Jo 5:5, I Co 2:3 15:43, II Co 12:9; pl., Mt 8:17, Lk 5:15 8:2, II Co 12:5 12:9, 10, I Ti 5:23, He 4:15.†
  SYN.: μαλακία, νόσος (v. DB, iii, 323a).
articulos.texto_es:
ἀσθένεια, -ας, ἡ
  (< ἀσθενής),
  [en LXX para
    כּשׁל, etc.;]
debilidad, flaqueza, enfermedad: Lk 13:11, 12, Jo 11:4, Ac 28:9, Ro 6:19 8:26, II Co 11:30 13:4, Ga 4:13( MM, s. v.), él 5:2 7:28 11:34; ἐν ἀ., Jo 5:5, I Co 2:3 15:43, II Co 12:9; plural, Mt 8:17, Lk 5:15 8:2, II Co 12:5 12:9, 10, I Ti 5:23, él 4:15.†
  SINÓNIMOS: μαλακία, νόσος (véase DB, iii, 323 a).

G378.definicion: to complete; by implication, to occupy, supply; figuratively, to accomplish (by coincidence ot obedience)
G378.definicion_es: completar; por implicación, ocupar, suplir; figuradamente, cumplir (por coincidencia u obediencia)

articulos.texto:
ἀνα-πληρόω, -ῶ,
  [in LXX chiefly for מלא, Le 12:6, al.; also שׁלם (Ge 15:16, III Ki 7:51, Is 60:20), etc.;]
1. to fill up, make full (in π. of completing contracts and making up rent; cf. MM, VGT, s.v.): τόπον, take one's place (cf. Heb. מָקוֹם מִלֵּא), I Co 14:16; άμαρτίας, complete the number, I Th 2:16; τ. νόμον, observe perfectly, Ga 6:2; pass., προφητεία, fulfilled, Mt 13:14.
2. to supply: τὸ ὑστέρημα, I Co 16:17, Phl 2:30 (Cremer, 838).†

G659.usos: cast off, lay apart (aside, down), put away (off)

articulos.texto:
ἀπο-τίθημι,
  [in LXX chiefly for נוּחַ hi.;]
to put off or aside; in NT always mid.,
   (a) to put off from oneself as a garment: τ. ἱμάτια, Ac 7:58; metaph., in ethical sense, to put of, lay aside: Ro 13:12, Eph 4:22, 25, Col 3:8, He 12:1, Ja 1:21, I Pe 2:1;
   (b) to stow away, put: ἐν τ. φυλακῇ (MM, s.v.), Mt 14:3.†

ἄρχω,
  [in LXX for חלל, משׁל, etc.;]
1. to begin.
2. to rule (v. DCG, ii, 538b.): c. gen., Mk 10:42, Ro 15:12. Mid., to begin: seq. ἀπό, Mt 16:21 20:8, Lk 14:18 23:5 24:27, 47, Jo 8:9, Ac 1:22 8:35 10:37, I Pe 4:17; c. inf., an Aramaic pleonasm, Mk 1:45 2:23 5:17, Lk 3:8, al. (v. M, Pr., 14 f.; Dalman, Words, 27; MM, s.v.).

ᾄδω (Attic form of Ion. and poët. ἀείδω),
  [in LXX chiefly for שִׁיר;]
to sing,
   (a) intrans., c. dat. (MM, VGT, s.v.), of praise to God: Eph 5:19, Col 3:16;
   (b) trans., c. cogn. acc.: ᾠδὴν, Re 5:9 14:3 15:3.†

G643.origen: de G575 (ἀπό) y un derivado de G4632 (σκεῦος)

articulos.texto:
ἀπο-σκευάζω,
  [in LXX: Le 14:36 (פּנה pi.)*;]
to pack and carry off; mid., to pack and remove one's goods: Ac 21:15, Rec. (v. ἐπισ-).†

G210.origen: de G1 (Α) (como negativa partícula) y G1635 (ἑκών)

articulos.texto:
ἄκων (Attic contr. for ἀέκων), -ουσα, -ον
  (< ἀ- neg., ἕκων, willing),
  [in LXX: Jb 14:17, II Mac 11:12*;]
unwilling: I Co 9:17.†

G737.usos: this day (hour), hence(-forth), here(-after), hither(-to), (even) now, (this) present

articulos.texto:
ἄρτι,
    adv.,
  [in LXX: Da LXX 9:22 10:11 (עַתָּה), al.;]
  adv., of coincidence, denoting strictly present time, as contrasted with past or future,
just, just now, this moment: Mt 3:15 9:18 26:53, Jo 13:7, Ga 4:20, I Th 3:6 (v. Lft., Notes, 44; Milligan, in l.), Re 12:10; opp. to past time, Jo 9:19, 25 13:33, I Co 16:7, Ga 1:9, 10; to future, Jo 13:37 16:12, 31, I Co 13:12, II Th 2:7, I Pe 1:6, 8; ἄχρι τῆς ἄ. ὥρας, I Co 4:11; ἕως ἄ., Mt 11:12, Jo 2:10 5:17 16:24, I Co 4:13 8:7 15:6, I Jo 2:9; ἀπ᾽ ἄ., v.s. ἀπάρτι (v. Rutherford, NPhr., 70 f; MM, s.v.).†
  SYN.: νῦν, now, "the objective, immediate present; ἤδη, now, already, "the subjective present, with a suggested reference to some other time or to some expectation". (Thayer, 75.)

G993.definicion: sons of commotion; Boanerges, an epithet of two of the apostles
G993.definicion_es: hijos de conmoción; Boanerges, un epíteto de dos del apóstoles

articulos.texto:
Βοανηργές, indecl. (on the derivation, v. Dalman, Gr., 144; Words, 42; Swete, Mk., l.c.; DCG, i, 216),
Boanerges: Mk 3:17.†
articulos.texto_es:
Βοανηργές, indeclinable (sobre la derivación, véase Dalman, Gr., 144; palabras, 42; Swete, Mk., l. con.; DCG, i, 216),
Boanerges: Mk 3:17.†

articulos.texto:
βεβαιόω, -ῶ
  (< βέβαιος),
  [in LXX: Ps 40 (41):12 (נצב hi.), 118 (119):28 (קוּם pi.), III Mac 5:42*;]
to confirm, establish, secure, of things (cl.): λόγον, Mk 16:[20]; ἐπαγγελίας, Ro 15:8; of persons (DCG, ii, 605): I Co 1:8, II Co 1:21. Pass., I Co 1:6, Col 2:7, He 2:3 13:9 (as an Attic legal term, to guarantee the validity of a purchase, establish or confirm a title; v. next word, Cremer, 139; cf. δια-β.).†

**† βήρυλλος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ,
  [in LXX: To 13:17 (-ύλλιον in Ex 28:20, שֹׁהַם)*;]
beryl, a jewel of sea-green colour: Re 21:20.†

† ἀγαλλίασις, -εως, ἡ
  (< ἀγαλλιάω),
  [in LXX (most freq. in Pss. and often coupled with εὐφροσύνη, as Ps 44 (45):15) chiefly for גִּיל;]
exultation, exuberant joy: Lk 1:44, Ac 2:46, He 1:9, Ju 24; χαρὰ καὶ ἀ., Lk 1:14 (Cremer, 592).†

Ἅγαρ (Rec. Ἄ-), ἡ, indecl. (in FlJ, Ἀγάρα, -ης, Heb. הָגָר),
Hagar (Ge 16): Ga 4:24, 25.†
articulos.texto_es:
Ἅγαρ (Rec. Ἄ-), ἡ, indeclinable (en FlJ, Ἀγάρα, -ης, hebreo הָגָר),
Hagar (Ge 16): Ga 4:24, 25.†

G833.origen: de la misma raíz que G109 (ἀήρ)
G833.definicion: a yard (as open to the wind); by implication, a mansion
G833.definicion_es: un patio (como abrir al viento); por implicación, una mansión

articulos.texto:
αὐλή, -ῆς, ἡ,
  [in LXX chiefly for חָצֵר;]
1. in Hom., an open courtyard before a house, hence, an enclosure in the open, a sheepfold: Jo 10:1, 16.

articulos.texto:
Α, α, ἄλφα (q.v.), τό, indecl.,
alpha, the first letter of the Greek alphabet. As a numeral, αʹ = 1, α͵ = 1000. As a prefix, it appears to have at least two and perhaps three distinct senses:
   1. ἀ- (before a vowel, ἀν-) negative, as in ἄ-γνωστος, ἄ-δικος.
   2. ἀ-, ἁ- copulative, indicating community and fellowship, as in ἁ-πλοῦς, ἀ-κολουθέω, ἀ-δελφός.
   3. An intensive force (LS, s. α), as in ἀ-τενίζω is sometimes assumed (but v. Boisacq, s.v.).

   (1) a messenger or delegate,
   (2) a bishop or ruler,
   (3) a guardian angel,
   (4) the prevailing spirit of each church, i.e. the Church itself. (Cf. Swete, Ap)., in l.; DB, iv, 991; Thayer, s.v.; Cremer, 18; MM, VGT, s.v.)

2. asirio en LXX, en el especial sentido de ángel, un espiritual, ser celestial, servidor sobre Dios y empleado como su mensajero a hombres, hacer conocido su propósitos, como Lk 1:11, o ejecutar ellos, como Mt 4:6. el ἄ. en Re 1:20 2:1, y otros, es de varios modos entendido como

articulos.texto:
αὐτός, -ή, -ό,
  determinative pron., in late Gk. much more freq. than in cl. (WM, 178 f.; Jannaris, HGG, §1399).
1. Emphatic (so always in nom. exc. when preceded by the art., v. infr., iii);
   (1) self (ipse), expressing opposition, distinction, exclusion, etc., αὐ. ἐκχυθήσεται, Lk 5:37; αὐ. ἐγινώσκεν, Jo 2:25; αὐ. ὑμεῖς, Jo 3:28; καὶ αὐ. ἐγώ, Ro 15:14; αὐ. Ἰησοῦς, Jo 2:24; αὐ. καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ, Mk 2:25; ὑμεῖς αὐ., Mk 6:31; esp. (as freq in cl.) αὐ. ὁ, Mt 3:4, Mk 6:17, Jo 16:27, I Th 3:11, al.; in late Gk., sometimes weakened, ἐν αὐτῇ τ. ὥρᾳ, in that hour, Lk 10:21 (M, Pr., 91; MM, s.v.);
   (2) emphatic, he, she, it (M, Pr., 86; Bl., § 48, 1, 2, 7), Mt 1:21 12:50, Lk 6:35, al.; pointing to some one as master (cl.), Mt 8:24, Mk 4:38, al.; αὐ., καὶ αὐ. = οὗτος, ὁ δε (Bl., § 48, 1), Mt 14:2, Mk 14:15, 44, Lk 1:22 2:28, al.
2. In oblique cases (cl.), for the simple pron. of 3rd pers., he, she, it, Mt 7:9, 10:12, 26:44, al.; with ptcp. in gen. absol., Mt 9:18, Mk 13:1, al. (for irreg. constructions, V. Bl., § 74, 5); pleonastically after the relative (cf. Heb. אֲשֶׁר לֹו; WM, 184 ff.; Bl., § 50, 4; MM, s.v.), Mk 7:25, Re 3:8, 7:2, al.; in constr. ad sensum, without proper subject expressly indicated, Mt 4:23, Ac 8:5, II Co 2:13, al.; gen. αὐτοῦ = ἐκείνου, Ro 11:11, I Th 2:19, Tit 3:5, He 2:4.
3. ὁ, ἡ, τὸ αὐ., the same: He 1:12, 13:8; τὸ αὐ., ποιεῖν, Mt 5:46, 47, al.; φρονεῖν, Ro 12:16 15:5, Phl 2:2, al.; τὰ αὐ., Ac 15:27, Ro 2:1, al.; κατὰ τὸ (τὰ) αὐ. (MM, s.v.), Ac 14:1, Lk 6:23, al.; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐ., together (MM, s.v.), Mt 22:34, Ac 1:15, al.; ἓν κ. τὸ αὐ., I Co 11:5, 12:11; c. dat. (cl.), I Co 11:5; with a noun, λόγος, Mk 14:39; μέτρος, Phl 1:30; πνεῦμα, I Co 12:4.
articulos.texto_es:
αὐτός, -ή, -ό,
  determinativo pronombre, en tardío griego mucho más frecuente que en en griego clásico (WM, 178 femenino; Jannaris, HGG, §1399).
1. enfático (así siempre en nominativo excepto cuando precedido por el artículo, véase abajo, iii);
   (1) sí mismo (ipse), que expresa oposición, distinción, exclusión, etc., αὐ. ἐκχυθήσεται, Lk 5:37; αὐ. ἐγινώσκεν, Jo 2:25; αὐ. ὑμεῖς, Jo 3:28; καὶ αὐ. ἐγώ, Ro 15:14; αὐ. Ἰησοῦς, Jo 2:24; αὐ. καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ, Mk 2:25; ὑμεῖς αὐ., Mk 6:31; sobre todo (como frecuente en en griego clásico) αὐ. ὁ, Mt 3:4, Mk 6:17, Jo 16:27, I Th 3:11, y otros; en tardío griego, a veces debilitado, ἐν αὐτῇ τ. ὥρᾳ, en que hora, Lk 10:21( M, Pr., 91; MM, s. v.);
   (2) enfático, él, ella, ello( M, Pr., 86; Bl., § 48, 1, 2, 7), Mt 1:21 12:50, Lk 6:35, y otros; que apunta a algún uno como amo (en griego clásico), Mt 8:24, Mk 4:38, y otros; αὐ., καὶ αὐ. = οὗτος, ὁ δε (Bl., § 48, 1), Mt 14:2, Mk 14:15, 44, Lk 1:22 2:28, y otros
2. en casos oblicuos (en griego clásico), para el sencillo pronombre de 3 º de la persona, él, ella, ello, Mt 7:9, 10:12, 26:44, y otros; con participio en genitivo absoluto, Mt 9:18, Mk 13:1, y otros (para irregular construcciones, véase Bl., § 74, 5); pleonásticamente después del relativo (compárese hebreo אֲשֶׁר לֹו; WM, 184 y ss.; Bl., § 50, 4; MM, s. v.), Mk 7:25, Re 3:8, 7:2, y otros; en construcción ad sensum, sin propio sujeto de modo expreso indicado, Mt 4:23, Ac 8:5, II Co 2:13, y otros; genitivo αὐτοῦ = ἐκείνου, Ro 11:11, I Th 2:19, Tit 3:5, él 2:4.
3. ὁ, ἡ, τὸ αὐ., el mismo: él 1:12, 13:8; τὸ αὐ., ποιεῖν, Mt 5:46, 47, y otros; φρονεῖν, Ro 12:16 15:5, Phl 2:2, y otros; τὰ αὐ., Ac 15:27, Ro 2:1, y otros; κατὰ τὸ (τὰ) αὐ.( MM, s. v.), Ac 14:1, Lk 6:23, y otros; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐ., juntos( MM, s. v.), Mt 22:34, Ac 1:15, y otros; ἓν κ. τὸ αὐ., I Co 11:5, 12:11; con dativo (en griego clásico), I Co 11:5; con un sustantivo, λόγος, Mk 14:39; μέτρος, Phl 1:30; πνεῦμα, I Co 12:4.

articulos.texto_es:
Ἀβιάθαρ, ὁ, indeclinable (hebreo אֶבְיָתָר),
Abiathar( I Ki 21:1): Mk 2:26.†

G46.origen: de G1 (Α) (como negativa partícula) y lo mismo que G1102 (γναφεύς)
G46.definicion_es: propiamente, sin abatanar, es decir, (por implicación) nuevo (dicho del paño)

articulos.texto:
*† ἄγναφος, -ον (= ἄγναπτος, < γνάπτω, late form of κνάπτω, to card wool),
uncarded, undressed, i.e. new (MM, VGT, s.v.): Mt 9:16, Mk 2:21.†

* ἀφρός, -οῦ, ὁ,
foam: Lk 9:39 (MM, s.v.).†

Ἁρμαγεδών (WH, Ἃρ Μαγεδών; Rec. Ἀρμαγεδδών, prop. = הַר מְגִדּוֹ), cf. LXX, Μαγεδών, II Ch 35:22, Μαγεδώ, Jg 1:27;
Har-Magedon (AV, Armageddon): Re 16:16 (v. Swete, in l., but also Thayer, s.v.).†
articulos.texto_es:
Ἁρμαγεδών (WH, Ἃρ Μαγεδών; Rec. Ἀρμαγεδδών, puntal. = הַר מְגִדּוֹ), compárese LXX, Μαγεδών, II Ch 35:22, Μαγεδώ, Jg 1:27;
Har-Magedon (AV, Armageddon): Re 16:16 (véase Swete, en l., pero también Thayer, s. véase .).†

G368.origen: de G1 (Α) (como negativa partícula) y supuesto derivado de un compuesto de G473 (ἀντί) y G4483 (ῥέω)

articulos.texto:
† ἀν-αντί-ρητος
  (T, -ρρητος), -ον (< ῥητός, spoken),
  [in Sm.: Jb 11:2 33:13*;]
not to be contradicted, undeniable: Ac 19:36 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

G986.origen: quizá lo mismo que la raíz de G985 (βλαστάνω)
G986.definicion: Blastus, an officer of Herod Agrippa
G986.definicion_es: Blastus, un oficial de Herod Agrippa

articulos.texto:
Βλάστος, -ου, ὁ,
Blastus, chamberlain of Agrippa: Ac 12:20.†

** ἅλυσις, -εως, ἡ,
  [in LXX: Wi 17:17*;]
a chain, bond: Mk 5:3, 4, Lk 8:29, Ac 12:6, 7 21:33 28:20, Eph 6:20, II Ti 1:16, Re 20:1.†
articulos.texto_es:
** ἅλυσις, -εως, ἡ,
  [en LXX: Wi 17:17*;]
una cadena, atadura: Mk 5:3, 4, Lk 8:29, Ac 12:6, 7 21:33 28:20, Eph 6:20, II Ti 1:16, Re 20:1.†

G96.origen: de G1 (Α) (como negativa partícula) y G1384 (δόκιμος)
G96.definicion: unapproved, i.e. rejected; by implication, worthless (literally or morally)
G96.definicion_es: no aprobado, es decir, rechazado; por implicación, sin valor (literal o moralmente)

articulos.texto:
ἀ-δόκιμος, -ον,
  [in LXX: Pr 25:4, Is 1:22 (סִיג)*;]
   1. of things (prop. of metals: LXX, Pr 25:4, Is 1:22), not standing the test, rejected: γῆ, He 6:8.
   2. Of persons, rejected after testing, reprobate: Ro 1:28, I Co 9:27, II Co 13:5-7, II Ti 3:8, Tit 1:16 (Cremer, 212).†

βάτος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ,
  [in LXX (always masc, as in Attic): Ex 3:2-4, De 33:16 (סְנֶה), Jb 31:40 (בָּאְשָׁה)*;]
a bramble-bush: Lk 6:44, Ac 7:30, 35; ἐπὶ τοῦ (τῆς) β., in the place concerning the bush: Mk 12:26, Lk 20:37.†

G829.origen: de G846 (αὐτός) y la raíz de G2237 (ἡδονή)
G829.definicion_es: complaciente consigo mismo, es decir, arrogante

articulos.texto:
αὐθάδης, -ες
  (< αὐτός, ἥδομαι),
  [in LXX: Ge 49:3, 7 (עַז), Pr 21:24 (יָהִיר)*;]
self-pleasing, arrogant: Tit 1:7, II Pe 2:10 (Cremer, 654).†
  SYN.: φίλαυτος (v. Tr., Syn., § xciii).

Βενιαμίν, (Rec. -μίν), ὁ, indecl.
    (Heb. בֶּנְיָמִין),
Benjamin: Ac 13:21, Ro 11:1, Phl 3:5, Re 7:8.†
articulos.texto_es:
Βενιαμίν, (Rec. -μίν), ὁ, indeclinable
    (hebreo בֶּנְיָמִין),
Benjamín: Ac 13:21, Ro 11:1, Phl 3:5, Re 7:8.†

G741.definicion: to prepare, i.e. spice (with stimulating condiments)
G741.definicion_es: preparar, es decir, sazonar (con condimentos estimulantes)

articulos.texto:
** ἀρτύω,
  [in Sm.: Ca 8:2*;]
1. to arrange, make ready (Hom.).
2. Of food (as in comic writers), to season (MM, s.v.): Mk 9:50, Lk 14:34, Col 4:6.†

G765.origen: de G1 (Α) (como negativa partícula) y supuesto derivado de G4576 (σέβομαι)
G765.definicion: irreverent, i.e. (by extension) impious or wicked
G765.definicion_es: irreverente, es decir, (por extensión) impío o malvado

articulos.texto:
ἀσεβής, -ές
  (σέβω, to reverence),
  [in LXX chiefly for רשׁע;]
ungodly, impious: Ro 4:5 5:6, I Ti 1:9, I Pe 4:18, II Pe 2:5, 6 3:7, Ju 4, 15.†
articulos.texto_es:
ἀσεβής, -ές
  (σέβω, a reverencia),
  [en LXX sobre todo para רשׁע;]
impío, impío: Ro 4:5 5:6, I Ti 1:9, I Peal 4:18, II Peal 2:5, 6 3:7, Ju 4, 15.†

articulos.texto:
ἀν-άπτω,
  [in LXX chiefly for יצת;]
to kindle: Lk 12:49, Ja 3:5 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†
articulos.texto_es:
ἀν-άπτω,
  [en LXX sobre todo para יצת;]
encender: Lk 12:49, Ja 3:5( MM, VGT, s. véase .).†

G306.origen: voz media de G303 (ἀνά) y G906 (βάλλω)

articulos.texto:
ἀνα-βάλλω,
  [in LXX: Ps 78:21 89:38 (עבר), I Ki 28:14, Ps 104:2 (עטה);]
to defer, put off (MM, VGT, s.v.): mid., Ac 24:22.†

G430.origen: voz media de G303 (ἀνά) y G2192 (ἔχω)
G430.definicion: to hold oneself up against, i.e. (figuratively) put up with
G430.definicion_es: sujetar a sí mismo arriba contra, es decir, (figuradamente) poner arriba con

articulos.texto:
ἀν-έχω,
  [in LXX chiefly for אפק hithp.;]
to hold up; in NT always mid., to bear with, endure: in cl. most freq. c. acc., but in NT c. gen. pers., Mt 17:17, Mk 9:19, Lk 9:41, II Co 11:1, 19, Eph 4:2, Col 3:13; seq. μικρόν τι, c. gen. pers. and c. gen. rei, II Co 11:1; c. dat. rei, II Th 1:4 (v M, Th., in l.); seq. εἴ τις, II Co 11:20; absol., I Co 4:12, II Co 11:4; to bear with = to listen to, c. gen. pers., Ac 18:14; c. gen. rei, II Ti 4:3, He 13:22 (cf. προσανέχω and MM, VGT, s.v.).†

G215.origen: de G1 (Α) (como negativa partícula) y un derivado de G2980 (λαλέω)

articulos.texto:
† ἀ-λάλητος, -ον
  (< λαλέω),
inexpressible, not to be uttered: Ro 8:26.†

† ἀγρεύω (ἄγρα),
  [in LXX: Jb 10:16, Pr 5:22 6:25, 26, Ho 5:2 (לקח ni., שׁחט, etc.)*;]
to catch or take by hunting or fishing; metaph., Mk 12:13.†

αἰσχύνω
  (< αἶσχος, shame),
  [in LXX chiefly for בּוּשׁ;]
   1. to disfigure (Hom.).
   2. to dishonour (Pr 29:15).
   3. to make ashamed (Si 13:7). Pass., to be put to shame, be ashamed: II Co 10:8; Phl 1:20, I Pe 4:16, I Jo 2:28; c. inf. (M, Pr., 205), Lk 16:3 (cf. ἐπ- (-ομαι), κατ-αἰσχύνω).†

* ἀντι-καλέω, -ῶ,
to invite in turn: Lk 14:12.†
articulos.texto_es:
* ἀντι-καλέω, -ῶ,
invitar en volver: Lk 14:12.†

G279.origen: de G1 (Α) (como negativa partícula) y supuesto derivado de G3340 (μετανοέω)

articulos.texto:
*† ἀμετανόητος, -ον
  (< μετανοέω),
1. impenitent: Ro 2:5
2. = ἀμεταμέλητος (π., Philo, al.; v. Deiss., BS, 257; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

G910.definicion: a baptizer, as an epithet of Christ's forerunner
G910.definicion_es: un bautizador, como epíteto del precursor de Cristo

articulos.texto:
*† βαπτιστής, -ου, ὁ
    (< βαπτίζω),
a baptizer: of John the Baptist, Mt 3:1 11:11, 12 14:2, 8 16:14 17:13, Mk 6:25 8:28, Lk 7:20, 33 9:19.†

G352.definicion: to unbend, i.e. rise; figuratively, be elated
G352.definicion_es: enderezarse, es decir, levantarse; figuradamente, animarse

G370.origen: de G1 (Α) (como negativa partícula) y G514 (ἄξιος)

articulos.texto:
ἀν-άξιος, -ον
  (ἀ- neg., ἄξιος),
  [in LXX: Je 15:19 א2 (זלל), Es 8:13, Si 25:8*;]
unworthy: c. gen., I Co 6:2 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

G489.origen: de un compuesto de G473 (ἀντί) y G3408 (μισθός)

articulos.texto:
*† ἀντιμισθία, -ας, ἡ
  (< ἀντίμισθος, for a reward),
a reward, requital: in good sense, II Co 6:13; in bad sense, Ro 1:27 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†
articulos.texto_es:
*† ἀντιμισθία, -ας, ἡ
  (< ἀντίμισθος, para una recompensa),
una recompensa, retribución: en sentido bueno, II Co 6:13; en sentido malo, Ro 1:27( MM, VGT, s. véase .).†
